label: Controlled by companion AI
summary: Whether the army is controlled by the companion AI.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the outliner (the side list of your units) and of the army window, one outliner element for the true case and another for the false case. The game does not explain the term 'companion AI' further.

label: Is embarked
summary: Whether the army is on board ships.
details: Vanilla adds an embarked icon after the army's name when it is, and the army window shows elements for an embarked army.

label: Is hostile to player
summary: Whether the army is an enemy of the player or hostile to the player.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

label: Is gathering
summary: Whether the army is still gathering its troops.
details: Going by its name and its use in the army window, where vanilla shows an element only while it is true.

label: Is hovered
summary: Whether the mouse pointer is over the army.
details: Going by its name only. No line names this exact function; the same name is used on characters and titles in the ledger and on coats of arms, which suggests the same kind of mouse-over check.

label: Is loot capped
summary: Whether the army has hit a cap on its loot.
details: Going by its name and its use in the map icon templates, where vanilla shows an element only while it is true. What the cap is comes from the name only.

label: Is moving
summary: Whether the army is currently moving.
details: Going by its name and its use in the shared tooltip file, where vanilla shows an element only while it is true.

label: Is neutral to player
summary: Whether the army is neutral towards the player.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

label: Is raid army
summary: Whether the army is a raiding army.
details: Vanilla uses it in the army window and the map icon templates to show elements only while it is true.

label: Recently disembarked
summary: Whether the army has just come off its ships.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

label: Is retreating
summary: Whether the army is retreating.
details: Going by its name only. No line names this exact function; vanilla uses a function of the same name on a unit item in the map icons and tooltips, which hints at the same meaning.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether the army is currently selected by the player.
details: Going by its name only. No line names this exact function; the same name is used on many other list items (saves, bookmarks, units) as a selection check.

label: Is sieging
summary: Whether the army is besieging a holding.
details: Vanilla uses it in the army window to show elements only while it is true.

label: Is bartering
summary: Whether the army is currently carrying out the barter action.
details: Vanilla uses it in the army window to show an element only while it is true. Bartering is the army option toggled elsewhere in the same window (see the ArmyWindow barter functions).

label: Is raiding
summary: Whether the army is currently carrying out the raid action.
details: Vanilla uses it in the army window to show an element only while it is true.

label: Army as script scope
summary: Turns the army into a script scope, so script-style links and values can be used on it in a text.
details: It is a 'promote' function: it returns a Scope object. The vanilla lines listed for the same name belong to other types (for example the player character), where it is used to call script values from a localization text. Not seen on an army in the given lines.

label: On mouse enter
summary: Tells the game that the mouse pointer has moved onto the army.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from an on_start hook in the map icon templates, paired with the mouse-leave function.

label: On mouse leave
summary: Tells the game that the mouse pointer has left the army.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from an on_start hook in the map icon templates, paired with the mouse-enter function.

label: The army itself
summary: The army itself, to hand over as an argument to another function.
details: The game does not name its return type. Vanilla uses it as an argument: to build a troop tooltip, to click an army group on the map, and to ask whether a knight is in this army.

label: Show AI order icon
summary: Whether the icon for the unit's AI order should be shown for the army.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

details: Vanilla uses it to set the pressed state of a button in the options window, and also to make that button ignore clicks.

details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click in the options window.

label: Set hiring manual
summary: Switches the hiring setting to manual.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click in the options window.

label: Turn setting flag on
summary: Switches the named automation setting (a flag) on.
details: It returns nothing and takes one argument, the setting's name as text. Vanilla calls it with 'raiding' and 'bartering' from button clicks.

fields.name: Arg0

details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

label: Set war attitude defensive
summary: Switches the war attitude setting to defensive.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

label: Set war attitude neutral
summary: Switches the war attitude setting to neutral.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, and it documents nothing more.

details: It returns nothing and takes one argument, the setting's name as text. Vanilla calls it with 'raiding' and 'bartering' from button clicks.

fields.name: Arg0

details: The game does not name its return type. The vanilla lines listed use the same function name on other objects (characters), so they do not show how a regiment uses it.
